data.title: YAML engine cursor re-anchor for durable long walks
data.goal: Split from 2026-09-27_0827-yaml-engine-to-leverage-s3-read-and-write by its decision D2. The yaml-adapter-engine re-anchors a cursor walk the way native FalconCollector does, so long collections (days) survive dead and corrupted cursors: proactive re-anchor after N pages from the watermark, re-anchor on listed 5xx statuses with a consecutive limit, an empty-page limit that ends the walk as truncated, and cursor-expiry detection in both shapes (HTTP 404 status line, and a 404 in the body errors under HTTP 200). Opt-in on cursor_recovery; non-opt-in behaviour unchanged.

lesson.statement: AidExtractor.ExtractAid can derive a unique key for a Discover asset that states no sensor AID.
lesson.outcome: Live full-inventory probe of 303 lab assets: 49 state an AID and the derivation produced a key for 0 of the remaining 254. The 32-hex suffix gate rejects the tenant's 56-char base64url token.
lesson.doNot: do not re-assume a derived AID keys an unmanaged Discover entity without probing that tenant's combined id shape first

lesson.statement: The Falcon checkpoint's boundary-key list has a ceiling that fails visibly if it grows.
lesson.outcome: The collector imposes no cap on that path and neither AdapterCheckpoint.AdapterState nor CommitPage documents one. Measured 460,022 bytes at a full 5,000-key set; it is pinned by a test, not capped.
lesson.doNot: do not assume a control artifact carrying a growable list is bounded because a sibling artifact is

lesson.statement: The Discover cursor leg observes a Falcon 404 as an HTTP 404 status line, so its re-anchor arm fires on an expired cursor.
lesson.outcome: No probe of the 404-under-200 behaviour was run in this task and the changed cursor leg was never exercised against one, so the re-anchor arm remains unproven on the code path this task edited. Four neighbouring beliefs stayed untested for a stated reason rather than an unexamined one: remediation-entity ordering is moot because the fallback key is the combined id verbatim, settings_hash is unreachable while prevention enrichment ships off, and device-entities batch membership is unchanged because it derives from the sensor AID, which is null for every AID-less host.
lesson.doNot: do not read an absent re-anchor count as evidence the cursor never expired; the vendor can deliver 404 under a 200 header

lesson.statement: Falcon findings never arrive without a matching asset in the same collection batch.
lesson.outcome: Zero orphans holds only at the default 2000-01-01 floor. The assets lane gates on last_seen_timestamp and the findings lane on updated_timestamp against the same floor, so a host not seen recently leaves the asset lane while its findings still pass: 3,342 orphans across 8 keys measured at --base-date 2026-08-30.
lesson.doNot: do not assume two independently-gated vendor lanes are mutually consistent without checking which vendor clock each one filters on

lesson.statement: A ~300 host and ~100k finding lab collection is short enough to re-run repeatedly during development.
lesson.outcome: Exactly one 236.2 s run exists and it was not repeated: it needs live credentials and would overwrite the batch the suite pins by name, and each run writes a 496 MB findings file.
lesson.doNot: do not plan an iteration loop around re-collecting from a live tenant when the suite pins a single batch by name

lesson.statement: In yaml-adapter-engine aabc8cf, pagination.expected_total_path asserts completeness only when a cursor walk ends by natural exhaustion, not at a max_pages cap; so it does not turn the Axonius bundle's max_pages 500 x limit 2000 truncation into a failure.
lesson.doNot: rely on pagination.expected_total_path to catch a walk that stopped at max_pages; the completeness check skips a max_pages stop, so set max_pages far above any tenant

lesson.statement: The Axonius get_devices cursor strategy reads meta.next_page only when it is a JSON string; any other JSON type ends the walk after page 1 with a success result.
lesson.doNot: assume a cursor pagination walk continues when the vendor cursor is not a JSON string; the engine stops after page one with success, so pair cursor strategy with expected_total_path

lesson.statement: yaml-adapter-engine at aabc8cf can merge records fetched from more than one endpoint into an arbitrary target record set (any earlier step, any number of sources, any join key) within one workflow.
citations: yaml-adapter-engine fa10015: empty aabc8cf to fa10015 diff of Definition/Logic (MergeIntoValidator, MergeJoinParser), Compile (StepFinalizer), MergeSourceFetcher, MergeEnrichmentSink; Workflow/Logic/Merging/MergeEnrichment.cs:217-249 (append); ME12
lesson.doNot: assume merge_into can merge several endpoints into an arbitrary target: each merge stage is its own lookup re-fetched per key batch, the target must be an earlier topic stage without for_each or poll, and the join is one key path

lesson.statement: Proceeding on unverified: merging PR 65 (181fd22) or its equivalent, which publishes every declared non-secret config_fields entry to the config template scope, changes no rendered request of any integration-yaml c424f0f unit.
citations: handoff 04-release-metadata/release-metadata.md:209-263; ledger RMC5/RME5; integration-yaml c424f0f bitsight/operations.yaml:28-35,84,152 and threatlocker/operations.yaml:18-20,51,91

yaml-adapter-engine origin/pr-65 diff aabc8cf..181fd22 Execution/Logic/ConfigFieldAliases.cs (declared loop, publish every non-secret field); fa10015 Execution/Logic/TemplateScopes.cs:17-32; Execution/Logic/OperationPlanFactory.cs:383-394; Workflow/Logic/WorkflowRunner.cs:92; Workflow/Logic/PlanExecutor.cs:57; cymulate-integration-adapters origin/dev YamlAdapter/Flows/WorkflowFlowRunner.cs:170-178 (WorkflowRun has no Config); integration-yaml c424f0f bitsight/operations.yaml:28-35, 84, 152 and flows/collect.yaml:16, 22; threatlocker/operations.yaml:18-20, 32, 51, 91 and flows/collect.yaml:17, 23; defender-vm/operations.yaml:32-44 (baseDate, sinceTime not declared); catalog search for config templates in every *.yaml
lesson.doNot: call an engine change to config publication (PR 65 or equivalent) request-neutral without listing every declared non-secret, non-aliased config field templated into a request path or header; bitsight and threatlocker change

lesson.statement: The load-time refusals that Falcon decision LD2 (task 2026-09-24_1141-aligning-falconcollector-and-its-yamladapter-counterpart, engine-policy-design.md 5.4) adds to MergeIntoValidator and MergeOptionsValidator would not run for the crowdstrike-falcon unit, because it is a folder unit whose merges live in flows/collect.yaml, and MergeIntoValidator reads only workflow.stages (MC4).

research/merge-recon.md section (3) defect; yaml-adapter-engine aabc8cf Definition/Logic/Validation/MergeIntoValidator.cs:24-26, Compile/Logic/ExplicitFlowExpander.cs:127-131, Definition/Logic/Loading/YamlIntegrationLoader.cs:202-232; integration-yaml crowdstrike-falcon flows/collect.yaml:27-65

constraint.statement: Source task: 2026-09-27_0827-yaml-engine-to-leverage-s3-read-and-write (read-only reference). Its accepted decisions PD7 (re-anchor keys: cursor_recovery.reanchor_after_pages, reanchor_on_status with max_consecutive_reanchors, pagination.empty_page_limit; counters in PaginationState, never checkpointed) and PD10 (second expiry arm: HTTP 200 with errors[] code equal to expiry_status and message matching expiry_message_contains; same ResetToWatermark action) are this task's design baseline. Its evidence FD1-FD3 (Falcon PDFs), FTC1 and FTC6 (native re-anchor and empty-page truncation), PE10 (EngineFailureClassifier.IsExpiredCursor gates on the status line), PC10 and PC11 (open: one work item fits; exhausted 5xx still reaches the classifier), K13, K21 and K22 apply. Read them with ailedger status/history on 2026-09-27_0827-yaml-engine-to-leverage-s3-read-and-write.

Branch from yaml-adapter-engine dev fa10015 without open PRs #65, #66, #67. PR #67 and task 2026-09-27_0827-yaml-engine-to-leverage-s3-read-and-write both change PaginationConfig.cs, integration.schema.json and CHANGELOG.md; whichever merges second rebases.

Opt-in only: the new keys and the second expiry arm apply only to operations that declare cursor_recovery. Every new plan-reachable property is nullable and ignored when null; PlanDigest, PlanJson and checkpoint bytes of every definition are unchanged. Known behaviour change for an existing unit: integration-yaml crowdstrike-falcon Spotlight operation (the only cursor_recovery user) now re-anchors on the documented 200-with-404-in-body expiry (spotlight.pdf p.19, 21); the contract states it.

Deliverable of this phase: current InternalRecon, PromptContract and OrchestrationPlan filed; no closeout; another agent implements. Official Falcon PDFs: cymulate-integration-adapters/src/Cymulate.Integration.Adapters/Collectors/FalconCollector/FalconDocs/OfficialDocs/. Id prefixes: operator C/E/D/K/ALT; recon RA*; designer RP*; orchestrator RO*.

claim.statement: The three re-anchor arms (depth, listed 5xx, both expiry shapes) and the empty-page limit fit one engine work item on the existing ResetToWatermark action, without a checkpoint change or a publishing-stage change.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If not, the item splits or needs a Design change before coding.

claim.statement: A 5xx response that has exhausted the operation's error_handling retries still reaches the page classifier on the production request path, so a status re-anchor arm can fire.
claim.consequenceIfWrong: If not, the 5xx arm never fires in production.

evidence.summary: WaitAndRetryAsync returns its final HTTP result after configured response retries; PageDispatcher sends the result to PageLoop, which reads and classifies it. Exception, cancellation, circuit-open and retry-delay-exceeded paths are distinct and can bypass response classification.

evidence.citation: yaml-adapter-engine fa10015 PageLoop.cs:179-216,283-373; CursorPaginator.cs:53-108; PaginationState.cs:23-67; OperationExecutor.cs:159-208; OperationResult.cs:11-86
evidence.summary: ResetToWatermark is in the page loop, accepted-page and paginator state paths are shared, and OperationResult has no explicit truncated stop reason. This supports the shared engine seam but leaves the exact truncation output contract for planning.

data.question: At fa10015, which engine pagination seams and existing lessons govern opt-in cursor re-anchor, exhausted 5xx classification, empty-page truncation, and unchanged non-opt-in identity?

newLessons.statement: A Falcon 404 always arrives as an HTTP 404 status line.
newLessons.outcome: No vendor evidence obtained. The defense was coded both ways instead and keys on body errors[] plus requested-minus-returned, never on status alone, so the belief no longer changes an outcome.
citations: verifier-2.md §2 A2; spotlight.pdf p19 via L-882455c1 (verifier) (verifier, 2026-08-27)
newLessons.doNot: Do not key a vendor-rejection defense on HTTP status alone; Falcon is documented to deliver a 404 under a 200 header on at least one endpoint.

artifact.title: Cursor re-anchor internal recon at fa10015
artifact.content:
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "taskId": "2026-09-28_0732-yaml-engine-cursor-reanchor",
  "claimSetHash": "cb6be68f5e8373a050b33f0be2637a3a62680432b15582a0312bc93fda0984de",
  "assessments": [
    {
      "claimId": "C1",
      "domain": "internal"
    },
    {
      "claimId": "C2",
      "domain": "internal"
    }
  ],
  "report": "# Internal Recon

Baseline: `yaml-adapter-engine` `dev` at `fa10015aebf5edcd2a54a6337bc5b2c0dc23a2be`, clean working tree. Roslyn loaded `Cymulate.Integration.Yaml.Engine.sln` (3 projects, none skipped). This is the Research-stage recon for claims C1 and C2; no product files were changed.

## Durable sources read

- `yaml-adapter-engine/CLAUDE.md` — engine layering, one type per file, public surface, sink ownership, and evidence rules.
- Source task `2026-09-27_0827-yaml-engine-to-leverage-s3-read-and-write` status: accepted PD10 amends superseded PD7; D2 splits this engine re-anchor task from stored sets. FDE1-FDE3 distinguish documented Spotlight 200-with-body-404 from undocumented Discover expiry shape. FTE1/FTE7 establish native re-anchor and empty-page truncation behavior. PE10 establishes the engine status-line gate.
- Current task constraints K1-K4 and projections — the opt-in and identity invariants are fixed by the operator. Recalled lesson `L-76ed5c8b` and newly served `L-33ce251b` reinforce PD10's two-shape detection; neither proves Discover's live response shape. GC1/GC2 bear on max-pages and cursor termination. Entity-id, tenant-scale, merge, and config-scope lessons do not govern this engine-only re-anchor design.

## Files in scope

- `src/Cymulate.Integration.Yaml.Engine/Pagination/Contracts/Models/PaginationConfig.cs`, `CursorRecoveryConfig.cs`, `PaginationState.cs` — nullable YAML keys and ephemeral counters; config/state worker.
- `src/Cymulate.Integration.Yaml.Engine/Definition/Schemas/integration.schema.json` — matching YAML declaration schema; config/state worker.
- `src/Cymulate.Integration.Yaml.Engine/Resilience/Logic/EngineFailureClassifier.cs` — opt-in HTTP 404 and 200/body expiry recognition, listed-status classification; runtime worker.
- `src/Cymulate.Integration.Yaml.Engine/Execution/Logic/Pages/PageLoop.cs`, `PaginationAdvancer.cs`, `src/Cymulate.Integration.Yaml.Engine/Pagination/Logic/Paginators/CursorPaginator.cs`, `src/Cymulate.Integration.Yaml.Engine/Execution/Logic/OperationExecutor.cs` — re-anchor trigger, page acceptance, empty-page stop and completion; runtime worker.
- `src/Cymulate.Integration.Yaml.Engine/Execution/Contracts/Models/OperationResult.cs`, `src/Cymulate.Integration.Yaml.Engine/Execution/Logic/OperationResultFactory.cs` — only if the explicit truncated outcome needs a public result signal; runtime worker owns that choice after plan definition.
- `tests/Cymulate.Integration.Yaml.Engine.Tests/Execution/EngineCursorRecoveryTests.cs`, pagination tests, `tests/.../Compile/PlanDigestTests.cs`, `PlanJsonRoundTripTests.cs`, loader/schema tests — contract-driven test worker; precise new test paths should be frozen in the plan.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — release note; assigned to one owner. No other repository is in implementation scope.

## Patterns to mirror

- Expiry classification → `EngineFailureClassifier.cs:21-42,273-297` — current precedence is recovery before body rules and generic 2xx success; current implementation checks HTTP status before body substring. For PD10, parse `errors[]` by code and message only when cursor recovery is configured, cursor active, and watermark available; malformed/unrelated bodies must fall through.
- Restart → `PageLoop.cs:179-216`, `CursorRecoveryTracker.cs:81-86` — `ResetToWatermark` drops cursor, sets recovery floor, repeats page; `RestartFromWatermark` retains initial floor if no watermark. The 5xx arm can reuse this action but needs its own consecutive budget and fallback to existing rule classification when exhausted.
- Retry boundary → `RetryPolicyFactory.cs:105-155`, `PageDispatcher.cs:34-65`, `PageLoop.cs:64-98` — `WaitAndRetryAsync` returns final HTTP response after response retry exhaustion; dispatcher passes it to the page loop for body read and classification. C2 validated by RAE1. Transport exception, caller cancellation, breaker-open, and delay-exceeded paths are separate and do not supply an HTTP response.
- Accepted page → `PageLoop.cs:283-373`, `PaginationAdvancer.cs:11-43`, `CursorPaginator.cs:53-108` — record count is post-recovery dedup before state advance; paginator creates a new state and copies watermark/floor but not prospective counters. Define whether empty-page counting uses raw mapped records or post-dedup records so re-anchor overlap pages do not falsely exhaust the walk.
- Completion → `OperationExecutor.cs:159-208`, `OperationResult.cs:11-86`, `OperationResultFactory.cs:105-141` — `Stopped` and `Exhausted` currently flow through completion; result exposes counts but no explicit stop reason or truncated flag. An empty-page limit cannot truthfully claim a distinct truncated outcome using current result shape alone. Plan an explicit observable result or a documented, testable failure/stop contract; do not conflate it with natural exhaustion.
- Identity → `PlanDigest.cs:20-27`, `PlanJson.cs:42`, `PaginationAdvancer.cs:25-43` — digest and JSON serialize the plan; resume sink receives cursor/offset/page plus existing recovery snapshot. New plan-reachable fields must serialize null as absent; new counters must remain in `PaginationState` and outside the sink snapshot.
- Existing tests → `EngineCursorRecoveryTests.cs:88,110,140` exercise status-line expiry, no-watermark and resume; `EnginePrefetchTests.cs:478` pins max-pages shortfall behavior. Add production-path cases for 200/body-404, malformed/unrelated bodies, exhausted 5xx after retry policy, consecutive budget, proactive depth, empty-page limit, and non-opt-in identity.

## Shared surface to freeze

- Exact YAML key names and defaults from PD7/PD10, nullable plan properties, validation bounds, and schema placement — config/state worker produces; runtime and test workers consume.
- Counter semantics: pages since anchor, consecutive status re-anchors, consecutive accepted empty pages; reset events and whether empty means pre- or post-dedup — runtime/test workers consume the frozen contract.
- Truncation observation contract at `OperationResult`/`PageOutcome` and checkpoint exclusion — runtime and test workers consume. This needs a plan decision before parallel implementation.

## Disjoint sets available

- Config and schema: `PaginationConfig.cs`, `CursorRecoveryConfig.cs`, `PaginationState.cs`, `integration.schema.json` — independent after shared key/counter contract is frozen.
- Runtime: classifier, page loop, paginator/advancer, outcome/result files if needed — independent of config/schema edits once the shared surface exists.
- Tests: new or dedicated test files under `tests/` — independent of production files once behavior and public contract are frozen. Existing test files should have a single owner if edited.
- Release note: `CHANGELOG.md` — isolated file, but can be assigned to the config owner without a separate worker.

## Landmines

- `CursorPaginator.UpdateState` creates a new state. Any new counter omitted from its copy silently resets per page (`CursorPaginator.cs:85-108`), so test a chain long enough to cross the configured threshold.
- Current 404 classifier matches a substring anywhere in a 404 body; PD10's 200 arm must inspect the same `errors[]` entry for matching code and message, not pair values from different entries (`EngineFailureClassifier.cs:273-297`).
- A 5xx re-anchor placed after `error_handling.rules` can be swallowed by a matching retry/defer/fail rule; PD7 requires bounded precedence followed by existing handling after exhaustion (`EngineFailureClassifier.cs:21-42`).
- `PageLoop` publishes before advancing; proactive re-anchor fires after an accepted page, with the next cursor live. Counting prefetch or a failed page would break the page threshold (`PageLoop.cs:315-373`). Prefetch is already loader-incompatible with recovery (`PaginationPrefetchValidator.cs:41`).
- A zero post-dedup count can occur on a legitimate boundary replay; the plan must define and test whether that counts toward empty-page truncation (`CursorRecoveryTracker.cs:37-79`).
- Non-opt-in identity is a byte-level requirement. Nullable properties alone do not establish unchanged JSON/digest; pin compiled PlanJson, PlanDigest and resume snapshot for representative non-opt-in definitions before and after.
- `PaginationConfig.cs`, schema and changelog overlap open PR #67 and source task work (K2); rebase the second merge, do not import either PR into this baseline.

## Claim assessment

- C1 — internal. RAE2 supports the common seam but does not prove the entire one-item design, especially truncation output and counter semantics. Leave open for planning and implementation evidence.
- C2 — internal, validated by RAE1 for an exhausted HTTP response. Exceptions and circuit-open are outside its stated response case.
"
}

decision.statement: Design baseline: the re-anchor keys of source-task PD7 (cursor_recovery.reanchor_after_pages; reanchor_on_status with max_consecutive_reanchors; pagination.empty_page_limit ending the walk as truncated; counters in PaginationState, never checkpointed) and the second expiry arm of source-task PD10 (HTTP 200 with errors[] code equal to expiry_status and message matching expiry_message_contains, same ResetToWatermark action). Opt-in on cursor_recovery; the existing expiry arm is unchanged.
decision.rationale: Operator accepted PD7 and PD10 in task 2026-09-27_0827-yaml-engine-to-leverage-s3-read-and-write (2026-09-27) and moved them here by its D2 (2026-09-28). Native parity (FTC1, FTC6), Discover treated as durable (K22 there), Phase 1 is 2-4 minutes so no checkpointing (K21 there).

constraint.statement: Contract run RP1 (reanchor-contract-designer): write prompt_contract.md and file PromptContract from RP1 for this task on D1, K1-K4 and RARECON1; settle or bound C1 with the truncation output contract and counter semantics (propose decisions with prefix RPD); include tests for every arm, both expiry shapes, unrelated and malformed 200 bodies, and the opt-in identity check; refresh the recon if claims change. Then stop.

decision.statement: Counter semantics for opt-in cursor recovery: reanchor_after_pages counts accepted pages since the last anchor, increments only after page acceptance and next-cursor extraction, and resets on ResetToWatermark; it fires when count reaches the configured positive threshold and the next cursor and watermark are live. max_consecutive_reanchors counts consecutive listed-status re-anchors, resets on any accepted page, and after the positive budget is exhausted the final response follows existing error rules. empty_page_limit counts consecutive accepted pages whose raw mapped record count is zero while the next cursor is live; reset on a nonempty accepted page or re-anchor; boundary replay pages with raw records but zero post-dedup records are nonempty. Counters stay in PaginationState only, survive paginator state replacement, and never enter checkpoint bytes.
decision.rationale: PD7 and PD10 fix the arms and native defaults; RARECON1 shows PageLoop acceptance and CursorPaginator state replacement. Raw count prevents re-anchor overlap dedup from falsely declaring truncation. The accepted-page boundary avoids counting retries and failed responses.

decision.statement: An opt-in cursor walk that reaches pagination.empty_page_limit with a live continuation cursor ends as an explicit pagination-truncated failure: OperationResult.Success=false and ErrorCode=PAGINATION_TRUNCATED, with a diagnostic ErrorMessage and the existing sink FailAsync path. It must not call sink CompleteAsync or report natural exhaustion; fetched and published counts remain accurate. Earlier published pages are not rolled back. Natural cursor exhaustion, including an empty final page with no next cursor, retains existing completion behavior. No new checkpoint or publishing-stage contract is introduced.
decision.rationale: RARECON1 and RAE2 show current Stopped/Exhausted completion has no explicit truncation signal; OperationExecutor.cs:179-234 routes failures to existing FailAsync and completion to CompleteAsync. A typed failed result prevents incomplete walks being accepted as complete while reusing the existing failure seam.

artifact.title: Cursor re-anchor execution contract
artifact.content:
Role:
You are a yaml-adapter-engine pagination and resilience engineer working from dev `fa10015`.

Goal:
Make opt-in cursor-recovery walks survive long collections by re-anchoring after a configured page depth, on configured final HTTP 5xx responses, and on expired cursors in either supported response shape. End a walk that repeatedly receives empty pages with a live cursor as explicitly truncated.

Context:
* This task is the engine-only re-anchor split accepted in source task `2026-09-27_0827-yaml-engine-to-leverage-s3-read-and-write` decision D2. Current task decision D1 carries source PD7 and PD10. `RARECON1` maps the engine seams at `fa10015`; claim C2 is validated by RAE1. C1 remains OPEN: the one-item/shared-seam design is plausible from RAE2 but must be proved during implementation.
* Falcon Spotlight documents an expired `after` token as HTTP 200 with `errors` code 404 (`spotlight.pdf` pp. 19, 21; source-task FD2/FDE2). Discover's exact expiry response shape is undocumented in the available PDFs (FD3/FDE3). Do not assume its 404 always appears on the HTTP status line. The existing integration-yaml CrowdStrike Spotlight operation declares `cursor_recovery` and gains the new body-expiry behavior when it uses this engine.
* Recalled lessons `L-33ce251b` and `L-76ed5c8b` warn against a status-only expiry assumption. `GC1`/`GC2` warn that a page cap or malformed continuation can appear complete. These are cautions, not new validated assumptions; the contract does not depend on their old claims being true.

Constraints:
* Implement only in `yaml-adapter-engine`, branching from clean dev `fa10015`; do not import open PRs #65, #66, or #67. `PaginationConfig.cs`, `integration.schema.json`, and `CHANGELOG.md` overlap PR #67 and the source task, so the second merge rebases.
* Keep the accepted opt-in keys from PD7/PD10: nullable `cursor_recovery.reanchor_after_pages`, nullable `cursor_recovery.reanchor_on_status` with nullable `max_consecutive_reanchors`, and nullable `pagination.empty_page_limit`. Omitted depth and empty-page limits disable their arms; native values 500 and 5 are reference values, not implicit engine defaults. When a status list is configured and its consecutive limit is omitted, use PD7's default budget of 5 without serializing that default into the plan. Positive limits and HTTP 5xx status entries require load-time validation. The new pagination key has effect only for a cursor-family operation that declares `cursor_recovery`.
* Preserve existing `cursor_recovery` eligibility rules: no publishing stage, merge target, or prefetch combination. Do not add a checkpoint field or change a publishing-stage path. All new plan-reachable properties are nullable and omitted from serialized plans when null. For every definition without the new keys, `PlanDigest`, `PlanJson`, and checkpoint bytes must remain unchanged; for definitions without `cursor_recovery`, runtime behavior remains unchanged.
* Follow RPD1 for counter semantics: depth counts accepted pages after the anchor and fires only when the next cursor and watermark exist; listed-status re-anchors have a separate consecutive budget reset by any accepted page, then fall through to existing error handling when exhausted; empty-page count uses raw mapped records, not post-recovery dedup, only while the next cursor is live. Reset empty and depth counters on re-anchor; copy all counters when the paginator replaces `PaginationState`. None are checkpointed.
* Follow RPD2 for truncation: the configured empty-page limit yields `Success=false`, `ErrorCode=PAGINATION_TRUNCATED`, a diagnostic error, and the existing sink failure path; never call completion or report natural exhaustion for that exit. Keep fetched/published counts honest and do not roll back already published pages. An empty final page without a live next cursor completes normally.
* Preserve the existing HTTP status-line expiry arm. Add an HTTP 200 arm only when recovery is enabled, an `after` cursor is active, and the required watermark exists: one `errors[]` entry must have code equal to `expiry_status` (JSON number or numeric string) and a message matching one configured `expiry_message_contains` substring case-insensitively. Use the same `ResetToWatermark` action. Malformed JSON, unrelated errors, values split across different entries, or an absent message are not expiry; they continue through existing classification.
* A configured listed 5xx is considered only after transport retry policy returns its final HTTP response. Within its positive budget, re-anchor before ordinary error rules; after budget exhaustion, let those rules decide. Exceptions, cancellation, circuit-open, and retry-delay-exceeded paths keep their existing handling.
* Do not use external live-tenant collection as a routine test. Official Falcon PDFs are under `cymulate-integration-adapters/src/Cymulate.Integration.Adapters/Collectors/FalconCollector/FalconDocs/OfficialDocs/` and are read-only references.

Success Criteria:
* Loader/schema accept valid opt-in keys and reject invalid limits, non-5xx status entries, and forbidden recovery placements or prefetch combinations without altering previously valid definitions.
* Production-path tests show depth re-anchor at exactly N accepted pages; no trigger on a failed, retried, or cursorless page; watermark/floor and dedup remain correct across state replacement and re-anchor.
* Production-path tests show a listed final 5xx re-anchors within the consecutive budget, acceptance resets that budget, and exhaustion reaches the existing error classifier. Test the retry-policy-to-page-classifier path, not a hand-built classifier-only response.
* Production-path tests show both HTTP 404 status-line expiry and HTTP 200 with a matching `errors[]` entry re-anchor. Test numeric and numeric-string codes, unrelated and malformed 200 bodies, cross-entry code/message mismatch, and non-opt-in 200 behavior.
* Production-path tests show `empty_page_limit` stops at exactly N accepted raw-empty pages with a live cursor as `PAGINATION_TRUNCATED`, never completes the sink, preserves counts, and resets on nonempty pages and re-anchor. A page emptied only by recovery dedup and an empty terminal page do not falsely truncate.
* A byte-level before/after fixture check proves unchanged `PlanDigest`, `PlanJson`, and checkpoint bytes for representative definitions without the new keys; an existing `cursor_recovery` definition with the keys absent remains behavior-compatible except for the documented Spotlight 200/body-404 expiry correction.
* Engine build and focused tests pass, followed by the project-appropriate suite. The execution record cites each check and its result. Independent verification and a fresh isolated paired code review cover the same frozen candidate before work is considered complete.

Execution Rules:
* Do not assume missing data. Treat C1 as OPEN until implementation and tests prove the shared engine seam and no checkpoint/publishing-stage change. If the design needs another work item, a checkpoint change, or a publishing-stage change, stop and return to Design rather than widening implementation.
